subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood / Acme Cloud
message_1_subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood / Acme Cloud
message_1_body:
Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through Acme Cloud's inference requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goals: lower per-token serving cost for inference-heavy batch jobs and reduce 95th-percentile latency for customer-facing prompts.
- Constraints: S3-hosted customer data, SOC 2 requirement for audit logs, and a tight procurement window for any vendor with dedicated capacity.
- What we showed: Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, prefix caching to cut token cost on repeated prompts, and the Shield (private) option for KMS-backed keys.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I attached the tailored pricing sheet (redwood-pricing-v2.pdf) and the recording from today's demo (redwood-demo-recording.mp4).
2) If the technical team wants a short spike, we can run a 2-week pilot on a small dataset (we handle infra and provide a simple eval harness).
3) Procurement: I can share standard contract redlines if legal wants them up front.

Are you still targeting a procurement decision by end of June? If so, I can coordinate the pilot + procurement checklist this week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: redwood-pricing-v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
Attachment: redwood-demo-recording.mp4 (MP4 link stub)

Bumping this — wanted to check whether procurement is still on track for end of June.

If it's easier, happy to put a short 20-min sync on the books to align on success criteria.

Thanks,
Marissa

Either way, quick note back is helpful — if you'd like, I can also introduce you to our Solutions Engineer (Aditya) for a short technical Q&A when you're ready.

Appreciate it,
Marissa
